subject: Post-demo: Acme bake-off — test plan & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: Acme bake-off — test plan & next steps

Hi John and Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the bake-off running:

Recap (from today’s demo)
- Goal: validate latency, cost/unit, and output quality of Redwood vs their existing hyperscaler endpoint on ACME workloads.
- Focus areas: end-to-end latency (p50/p95), throughput per reserved capacity, API compatibility (tool-calls & streaming), and quality regressions on representative prompt set.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Confirm owners & infra: ACME to provide S3 access or sample dataset; Redwood to provision dedicated test pool. (see attachments)
2) Run initial baseline tests vs Hyperscaler A and Hyperscaler B — Redwood will provide comparison matrix and recommended config.
3) Success criteria (draft): p95 latency <= 450ms on typical prompt mix, throughput supporting 3k tokens/min sustained per reserved instance, and no >5% quality regression on the named eval set.
4) Timeline: kickoff this week, smoke tests by 12/3, full bake-off completed by ~12/10.

Attachments: acme-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx (owners/timeline), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf (high-level differentiators).

Please confirm owners for: S3 access / test data, procurement contact for trial capacity, and a preferred kickoff window (we suggested 12/2–12/3). Happy to adjust the success thresholds after your input.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Acme bake-off — test plan & next steps (technical details)

John / Priya — looping in technical details and owners from Redwood. Answers inline to your questions above.

Q1 (p95 target): that threshold is intended for steady-state (warm instances). We’ll clearly separate cold-start measurements in the report. Suggested measurement windows: 5-minute warm steady-state and 1-hour sustained throughput run.

Q2 (model parity): to be maximally fair we recommend two comparison modes:
- Mode A (apples-to-apples): run the same open model binary with identical precisions/kv cache behavior on both endpoints.
- Mode B (production parity): run Redwood with our optimized quantized runtime (same model family) to show production economics.

Technical test plan highlights (owners):
- Redwood infra provisioning & orchestration (owner: aditya_rao) — provision dedicated test pool + routing rules.
- Model & quantization config (owner: vanessa_ortiz) — responsible for quant config and kernel selection.
- Eval harness & quality metrics (owner: marissa_cole) — prompt sets, scoring rubric, and reporting.
- Data transfer & ingestion (owner: John Doe / ACME) — S3 bucket + sample inputs.

Success metrics (concrete):
- Latency: p50/p95 (steady-state) for the canonical prompt set. Target p95 <= 450ms.
- Throughput: sustained tokens/min at target latency (goal: 3k tokens/min per reserved instance).
- Cost: token/unit cost delta vs Hyperscaler measured over 72-hour run.
- Quality: automatic eval + manual spot checks; regression threshold <=5% on key metrics.

Smoke test plan (this week):
- 12/2 AM PT kickoff: verify credentials, confirm S3 + sample data, run smoke 5-min warm window.
- 12/3: baseline runs against Hyperscaler A (Mode A).
- 12/7–12/9: production parity runs (Mode B) + final comparison matrix.

Attachments: I uploaded an initial XLS with owners and a short runbook (see acme-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx).

If that looks good I’ll provision the pool and share ephemeral API keys + a runbook for the tests.

—Aditya
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
